# Windows scroll performance — blueprint

**Goal:** Smooth native wheel, trackpad, keyboard, and touch scrolling without changing the visual direction of the editorial portfolio. The modern source is `dist/lab/modern/` and the homepage is generated by `scripts/render-portfolio.mjs`. Avoid adding Lenis or intercepting native wheel events.

## Source-level diagnosis (not measured Windows hardware FPS)

- `modern.mjs`: WebGL gallery skipped frames for 32 ms (~30 FPS), with 13/s exponential delayed movement.
- `effects.mjs`: experience canvas skipped frames for 45 ms (~22 FPS); chapter reveal blended only across the middle 30% of each scroll interval.
- `showcase-renderer.mjs`: WebGL requested `powerPreference: 'low-power'`, which can select a lower-performance adapter on some systems.
- `showcase-mist.mjs`: a fixed blurred Canvas is painted on the main thread, which warrants profiling if jank persists.

## Patch 1 (this branch)

1. Update the WebGL coil on rAF cadence, with a ~12 ms minimum; preserve ~30 FPS for slower Canvas fallback.
2. Broaden chapter transitions to 84% of the interval; time-smooth visual chapter progress at 22/s without modifying scroll position.
3. Raise the gallery damping response to 20/s; let the browser choose its default GPU rather than explicitly selecting low-power.
4. Add pure interpolation/pacing tests and preserve existing lifecycle, resource, reduced-motion, and offscreen cleanup tests.
5. Keep the main homepage markup, visual copy, mobile layout, and scroll interactions unchanged.

## Validation before merge

Run:
```sh
node scripts/test-scroll-timing.mjs
node scripts/test-gallery-lifecycle.mjs
node scripts/test-gallery-resources.mjs
node scripts/render-portfolio.mjs --check
```

Manual matrix: Win 11 Chrome/Edge + traditional wheel, Win trackpad when available, macOS Safari/Chrome, mobile touch, reduced motion, WebGL-disabled Canvas fallback. Scroll the Experience and Work sections; use section buttons, reverse-scrolling, links into project details, and final-image handoff.

Capture Chrome Performance recordings before/after, dropped frames and long tasks. Use `?gallery-profile` to inspect `document.querySelector('.gallery-stage').dataset.galleryProfile` and `.dataset.renderer`; the profile measures CPU submission time, *not* actual GPU paint time.

**Performance objective (not yet verified):** ~55+ visually complete frames/s on capable 60Hz Windows hardware for the timeline and WebGL gallery; avoid skipping large portions of chapter transitions on ordinary wheel input. Canvas fallback deliberately favors lower frame rate over page responsiveness.

## Follow-up if the first patch is insufficient

Profile the main-thread mist renderer, the 30 FPS hero worker, GPU texture upload churn during sudden project changes, and Windows GPU selection. Prefer adaptive rendering and reduced overdraw over arbitrary scroll-wheel smoothing.
